turns.learner: Hello! I want to practise working out why a text was written. I think it's mostly about the topic, right?
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good to see you. Let's test that idea together.

Think about the topic "rain". Here are two short texts about it, which are my own examples:

A: "Rain falls when water in clouds becomes heavy."
B: "Rain is wonderful, so you really must visit our rainy island this year!"

Both texts are about rain. Do you think the writer wanted to do the same thing in both texts? Tell me what you think, in your own words, and why.

turns.learner: I think yes, the same. Both are about rain, so both writers want to inform us about rain.
turns.tutor:
Thank you for explaining your reasoning. You said both writers "want to inform us about rain", and for text A that may fit.

Let's check text B more closely. The topic is not the only clue. Look at the exact words the writer chooses in B, especially "wonderful" and "you really must".

Read B again slowly. Do those words sound the same as the words in A? Then tell me again: did both writers want to do the same thing?

turns.learner: B sounds more excited. Maybe it wants me to visit the island? But the topic is still rain, so I'm not sure.
turns.tutor:
Good noticing. You said B "sounds more excited" and "wants me to visit the island". That is a careful reading of the text.

I have one question about your thinking. Which exact words in B made you think the writer wants you to visit?

Please quote the words from B. Then tell me if text A has any words like that.

turns.learner: The words 'you really must visit'. Text A has no words like that, it just says facts. So maybe B is persuading, A is informing?
turns.tutor:
Yes. You quoted "you really must visit" and noticed that A "just says facts". That is how to decide: the writer's words show the purpose, not only the topic.

Now try this question.

Why did the writer write this text? Give one word, such as inform, persuade, warn or complain.

turns.learner: Which text do you mean? I don't see a new one. Maybe text B, so persuade?
turns.tutor:
Sorry, I did not give you a text. Thank you for asking.

Here is a new short text. It is my own example, so please do not use text B.

"Please be careful. The path near the river is very wet, and visitors can easily fall."

Read the exact words the writer chooses. Why did the writer write this text? Give one word, such as inform, persuade, warn or complain.

turns.learner: Inform? It tells us about the path by the river. But 'be careful' sounds a bit different, I'm not sure.
turns.tutor:
Good that you noticed "be careful" sounds different. Trust that feeling.

Here is a general idea. A writer's words often show what the writer wants the reader to think, feel or do. The topic alone does not show this.

Look again at "Please be careful" and "visitors can easily fall". In your own words, what does the writer want the visitors to do, or to avoid? Then choose one word for the purpose again.
